# R383 — decode NT1 native activation quantization and reuse audit

Date: 2026-10-13 (Asia/Tokyo). Read-only source and primary-source scan. Fixed worktree `/home/yayoi/ghq/github.com/yqYo1/Strata/.worktree/feat-phase-cache-stock-bench-20261013`, HEAD `499f226a0f3b46aa1bdcd0314fd0f81558799f6f` as supplied. Latest phase-OFF registry provenance supplied: `bench/results/2026-10-13-upstream-benchsh-phase-off-control/report-registry-v189.json`, exact 922. Consulted existing R370v2, R371v2, R369v2, CPU expert audit chain and R380/R381. No code, Git, build, test, import, GPU/model, profiler, process/service, or cleanup action. No timing or performance claim.

## Finding

For the common NT=1 decode case, the input activation quantization is already prepared once per token and layer before the experts are grouped into CPU jobs. Each selected expert job points at that same prepared row. There is no per-expert or per-worker duplication of the GU input quantization to amortize in this route, and there is no missing reusable input cache to add. The quantized input lives in a dispatch-owned per-token buffer for the synchronous layer dispatch; pool workers only read its pointer while the batch is running. This finding is distinct from the intermediate FF activation: that value is expert-specific because each expert has different gate/up weights and SwiGLU output, so its down-projection activation must be quantized per expert (and per token).

## Source path and ownership

`src/core/expert_source.cpp:1918-1926` first checks that there is at least one CPU-routed entry, then prepares all `n_tok` inputs once: for the native Q2_0 gate/up special case it calls `act_quant_any` into `d.act_multi[t]`; otherwise it calls `native_quant_act(fmt, x_f[t], d.nact_multi + t*kNativeActBytes)`. Thus an all-GPU layer skips host preparation entirely, while a CPU-served layer prepares one image per token, not one per selected CPU expert.

At `src/core/expert_source.cpp:1960-1978`, routing walks token/expert entries and merges repeated expert IDs into one `ExpertJobMulti`, with `jb.nt` and each token's output row. Every job's `act[t]` points to `d.act_multi[t]`, and every native job's `nact[t]` points to the same `d.nact_multi[t]`. For an NT1 job there is one activation pointer, shared across the GU rows of that job. Across ten distinct experts the pointer remains identical for that layer/token. `ExpertJobMulti` documentation in `include/strata/kernels/cpu/pool.hpp` confirms `nact` is a layer-native activation image per token; `native_expert.hpp` documents `vec_dot_type` activation conversion.

The object lifetime is sufficient: buffers are members of the persistent `ExpertDispatch`, and `expert_pool_dispatch_multi` does not return until after `run_split_multi_native` has completed the CPU batch. `pool.cpp:470-508` publishes the jobs, runs GU, forms expert-specific intermediate quantizations, runs Down, and only then returns. The pool has no persistent input-layout cache because the existing dispatch buffer already supplies the reusable input for the entire batch.

The separate non-native single-token `ExpertJob` path also stores a pointer to one shared `d.act` in each expert job; `include/strata/kernels/cpu/pool.hpp` documents that sharing. This is consistent with, but not needed to establish, the native NT1 multi-job finding.

## Which activation representation is actually consumed

`native_fmt` in `src/kernels/cpu/native_expert.cpp:31-72` asks GGML CPU type traits for both weight types' `vec_dot_type`, requires a `from_float` converter, checks block divisibility, records activation byte sizes, and rejects oversized images. `native_quant_act` at lines 83-85 dispatches either the Q8_K AVX2 quantizer for Q8_K when enabled or the type trait's quantizer. The corresponding `native_gu_rows` obtains the weight type's `vec_dot` and passes the prepared activation pointer to that dot (`native_expert.cpp:129-148`). These contracts are quantized-input contracts; the generic supported native GU path does not feed an FP32 activation vector to the row dot.

The notable exception is the local GGUF Q2_0/type-42 gate/up kernel. It uses Strata `ActQ`, not GGML's native image: source comments at `src/core/expert_source.cpp:1655-1703` and `src/kernels/cpu/pool.cpp:452-465` explicitly guard the `act` pointer for that case. The layer-level `act_quant_any` is still performed once per token and shared. For other formats, `act` may be null and the kernel reads `nact`.

The intermediate is a different boundary: `pool.cpp:491-500` quantizes each `split_multi_[e].ff[t]` into that expert's own `hq[t]` (or Q2 `ActQ`) between GU and Down. Pool buffers are indexed by expert and token. Because the FF row depends on the expert's own gate/up weight rows, pooling these values across distinct experts would be incorrect. The R371 source summary likewise identifies GU input conversion once per layer/token and FF conversion once per expert/token.

No raw-FP32 vec-dot fast path was found in this native ExpertJobMulti route: admission requires a CPU `vec_dot` and the corresponding activation `vec_dot_type`'s `from_float`; preparation converts into that representation. This conclusion is scoped to the native expert dispatch inspected here, not every CPU kernel in Strata.

## Synchronization and activation lifetime

The CPU job path is synchronous at the `ExpertDispatch` call boundary. For the segmented verifier route, `src/core/verify.cpp:1567` waits for `stream_sync(cs_)` before invoking the CPU pool callback, then after callback dispatch synchronizes the copy stream at `1599`. The callback reaches `drive_pool_multi`/`expert_pool_dispatch_multi` (`src/program/generate.cpp:834-839`) and the source prepares activations and invokes the pool before returning. This makes the input-ready handoff and the host CPU lifetime ordered in the target segmented path; this report does not generalize that to unsegmented concurrent-USM polling. The single-token session path has an event completion before callback (`src/core/session.cpp:702`), as recorded in R370v2.

## Amortization decision

Reject an input activation reuse/cache proposal for this NT1 route: the observable duplicate count in the inspected source is zero. A layer-wide or per-worker cache would duplicate existing dispatch ownership and add state/lifetime complexity without removing quantizer invocations. The accurate quantization work denominator is CPU-served tokens per layer, not routed experts: for NT1 with ten selected experts, one source activation image feeds those expert jobs. If only some routes go to CPU, the current code still prepares one image for each token whenever any CPU route exists; that may merit measurement only if existing `actq` accounting shows meaningful cost, but it is not per-expert repetition.

The intermediate quantization remains one image per distinct CPU expert/token, a structurally distinct and legitimate operation. Existing pool accounting separates its host-side interval as `ms_multi_q`; the outer dispatch also accumulates input preparation in `d.ms_actq`. These counters are the minimal existing measurements to inspect if quantizer cost attribution is needed. Because input quantization is already one-time and can overlap/compete with GPU work, a speed claim needs phase and request-level timings under the official paired benchmark, which was explicitly not run here. A new profiler counter is not warranted to substantiate duplicate work when source shows there is none. If existing counters do not expose enough attribution, use a matched diagnostic of `d.ms_actq` deltas by `n_tok` and CPU-served layer count, plus `ms_multi_q` per distinct job-token; do not add counters inside worker loops or infer the quantizer as a bottleneck.

## External primary implementation context

The official llama.cpp/ggml CPU implementation is the relevant format-contract reference: its type traits define the weight `vec_dot` and associated activation `vec_dot_type`/`from_float` pairing used by the inspected Strata adapter. See [ggml-cpu.c](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ggml-cpu.c) and the [ggml CPU x86 sources](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/tree/master/ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/x86). The source-level reusable object here is the already-quantized activation pointer passed to multiple expert dot products; no external project result establishes a further benefit for Strata's target. No new AVX2 quantizer or prepared-layout-cache proposal is supported by this audit.

## Limits and prior-report delta

This is a source ownership and call-count conclusion, not a measured quantizer-cost conclusion. It does not establish that all ten selected experts are CPU-served; GPU/PCIe residency can reduce CPU jobs. It does not infer physical memory traffic or DDR ceilings from logical bytes. R371 already states the input Q8_K image is 2,920 B/token at H=2560, but its small logical size alone does not prove cache residency or negligible cost. R370v2 supplies the safe callback/synchronization boundary. R369v2's logical-byte caveat remains in force. The distinct expert-specific FF/down activation boundary is documented here to prevent conflating it with reusable layer input.
